name: Isla del Bluencanto (Puerto Rico)
commemorates: Puerto Rico: JetBlue's service to the island.
description: Fuselage: JetBlue blue, plain ahead of the wing; from the wing aft it's covered in tropical art on the blue: orange flowers, pink-red flowers, a fan of yellow banana leaves, big orange fruits, a cluster of red berries, pale-green leaves, and light-blue and navy stripes round the tail cone. 'jetBlue' in white over the forward windows; '¡SOMOS BORICUA!' large in white on the belly. Tail: a jíbaro (a Puerto Rican countryman in a yellow straw pava hat and a light-blue shirt) among teal palm fronds on the blue fin. Engines blue. Designed by Puerto Rican artist Juan Gutiérrez Rovira (The Stencil Network), chosen by public vote.

sources.title: JetBlue: Isla del Bluencanto release (Business Wire, 2025-10-02)
sources.note: A320 N657JB 'Isla del Bluencanto', unveiled at San Juan in October 2025: designed by Puerto Rican artist Juan Gutiérrez Rovira (The Stencil Network), chosen by public vote; 'Somos Boricua' on the belly. JetBlue's second Puerto Rico livery after Bluericua (2018).

lightBlue.name: tail cone and shirt light blue

logos.description: The tropical art aft of the wing, first of eight pieces along the body (the art is cut into pieces so each stays inside the tapering fuselage): orange flowers low by the wing, pink-red flowers with pointed petals, and the front of the yellow banana leaves.
The tropical art, piece 2: the fan of yellow banana leaves.
The tropical art, piece 3: big orange fruits and teal leaves ahead of the aft door.
The tropical art, piece 4: orange fruit by the aft door and the cluster of red berries.
The tropical art, piece 5: red berries and pale-green leaves under the fin.
The tropical art, piece 6: pale-green leaves and the start of the light-blue tail cone.
The tropical art, piece 7: the light-blue tail cone with navy stripes across it.
The tropical art, piece 8: the tail cone's end.

A jíbaro, a Puerto Rican countryman, from the chest up and filling the fin: a wide yellow straw pava hat, his face turned a little toward the nose and looking down, shown in salmon highlights on the dark blue, a moustache, a light-blue collared shirt, one hand raised in front of his chest; teal palm fronds fan out behind him.
A small US flag ahead of the registration over the rear windows.

titles.style: The jetBlue wordmark in white over the forward windows.
Large white rounded capitals along the belly, seen from below.

notes: Drawn from one photo from below and behind the left wing (N657JB at Fort Lauderdale; the file's title dates it 2025-11-17, its metadata 2026-10-17). An art livery: the art is described as logos (docs/LOGOS.md), not drawn as areas, so the fuselage and fin stay blue here; their places are measured on the photo. The crown isn't seen from below. Re-checked 2026-11-27: the pink-red flowers are warmer than first written (#EC456F, was #D2408A) in the sunlit photo; the earlier block areas (flowers, leaves, fruits, berries, tail cone, fronds, hat, face, shirt) gave way to the logos. The belly reads '¡SOMOS BORICUA!' (JetBlue's release; the lead called the jet 'Yo Soy Boricua'); its direction (which end it starts) isn't certain from an oblique view. 'Isla del Bluencanto' (the aircraft's name, small white script under the cockpit) and the registration aren't drawn. The right side isn't seen.
